scope: Discrete-cycle teaching model, scalar differential checks, arithmetic and predictor; optional official RARS encoding/architecture, never real hardware timing or Ripes GUI.
scenarios: ALU chain without forwarding waits four cycles and keeps result
Load-use freezes ID while load advances and EX receives a bubble
Nearest matching writer wins over an older matching writer
A newer load masks an older same-register ALU value until ready
Same-cycle WB then ID read needs no stall without forwarding
Store data is captured in EX and immediate load-store needs one stall
Taken branch removes both younger instructions and all their effects
Untaken path executes its store; final load is not the transient 99
Load-branch stall followed by flush preserves data and target result
Reordered independent work preserves registers and data memory
x0 and I-immediate bit positions do not create false dependencies
A flushed unsupported word is never decoded or executed
Executed unsupported code and misaligned data fail explicitly
Finite empty/single programs and infinite loop bounds
Two hundred generated dependent arithmetic programs, both forwarding modes
Two-bit predictor follows all state transitions and saturation
Predict before update: T,T,N,T has two errors from weak not-taken
Two repeated T,T,T,N loops differ for one and two bits
Alternating history and empty input do not promise universal gains
Time units, weighted CPI and whole-work speedup examples
Dynamic loop count includes final branch but excludes output region
Amdahl time fractions and finite pipeline overhead
